result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: Jobs::PollFeed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` straight into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Post#cook then `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Unlike import_remote, which whitelists via Readability's tags/attributes options, the PollFeed path never sanitizes feed content, so arbitrary feed markup would be stored and executed in readers' browsers on the embedding site's origin.

judged_text: The raw_html sanitization contract is enforced by only one of TopicEmbed.import's two callers — import_remote whitelists markup through Readability's tags/attributes options, while PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight into import where Post#cook returns it verbatim as cooked. Whatever markup the feed carries — script, iframe, on* event handlers — is stored as the post's cooked HTML and rendered unescaped to every reader on the Discourse origin, so any feed author (or feed hijacker) bypasses the whitelist the other path establishes and executes script in readers' browsers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` constrains HTML via Readability tag/attribute whitelists, but `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly to `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) with no sanitization; `scrub` only addresses invalid encoding, not hostile tags/attributes. Therefore a feed item containing `<script>`, `<iframe>`, or `on*` handlers would be stored and served as cooked HTML, leading to XSS on the Discourse origin.
